This is the forge-neutral, process-neutral core that SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001B (CLI command modes) and SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C (GitHub Actions topology) both build on, so that a reviewed versioning decision can survive a process boundary without a CI cache, an untracked workspace file, or a silently recomputed fresh plan being treated as authoritative release intent.",
  "scope": "A new `PublishPlanEnvelope` type in `crates/callisto-model/src/envelope.rs` wrapping the existing `PublishPlan` (crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:27) as its payload; the canonical JSON encoding used for digest computation; the exhaustive, deterministically ordered input sets for `configDigest` and `inputDigest`; the accepted `schemaVersion` / `digestSchemeVersion` values and the rejection behavior for every other value; the total structural validation performed before any consumer mutates state; and a structural provenance table proving every envelope field is sourced from repository content or static configuration rather than the process environment. Digest computation and validation are pure functions of on-disk state plus the envelope bytes: they read no credentials, spawn no registry client, and perform no planning pass.",
  "non_goals": [
    "Implementing the CLI command-mode separation, the plan-driven execution entry point, or the operation-status record. SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001B owns those; this spec defines only the envelope and the validation function they invoke.",
    "Implementing any forge job topology or artifact handoff. SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C owns that.",
    "Including `callisto_graph::plan::VersionPlan` (crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs:13) in the envelope. At last_verified_revision it derives only `Clone, Debug, Default` -- no `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, or `JsonSchema` -- `callisto-graph` carries no `schemars` dependency, and `plan_publish` consumes it purely as an in-process intermediate (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:215-234, reading only `plan.bumps`). It is never serialized and is not part of the durable contract; the envelope payload is `PublishPlan` alone.",
    "Cryptographically signing or attesting the envelope. The digests here bind a plan to observed disk state; they establish neither authorship nor non-repudiation, and no signature, in-toto attestation, or provenance statement is produced.",
    "Committing transient plan files, CI outputs, or caches to the repository.",
    "Replacing committed manifests, changelogs, release tags, or registry state as the durable records of a completed release. The envelope records intent; those remain the record of outcome.",
    "Unifying the two `pre.json` read paths. `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs:79` hardcodes `.changeset/pre.json` while the delete path at version.rs:254 resolves `[changesets].dir`; AC-002 hashes both paths so the digest is faithful to today's behavior, but reconciling the inconsistency is a separate change."
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-001",
      "criterion": "The serialized envelope is `PublishPlanEnvelope` (crates/callisto-model/src/envelope.rs), `#[serde(rename_all = \"camelCase\", deny_unknown_fields)]`, with exactly these fields: `schemaVersion` (u32, governs the envelope), `digestSchemeVersion` (u32), `sourceCommit` (the 40-character lowercase-hex git HEAD SHA observed at planning time, the same value `Workspace::git_access().head_sha()` returns at crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs:254), `configDigest` (64 lowercase hex characters), `inputDigest` (64 lowercase hex characters), `generatedAt`, and `plan` (a `PublishPlan`, which retains its own `schemaVersion` field, crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:28). `generatedAt` is RFC 3339 in UTC at whole-second precision with a literal `Z` suffix and no fractional part -- exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, e.g. `2026-08-29T14:03:11Z`. `digestSchemeVersion` is incremented whenever the hashed input set or the canonicalization procedure changes, independently of `schemaVersion`, so a future config-shape change cannot silently produce a mismatched digest that wrongly accepts or rejects a plan. `PublishPlanEnvelope`, `PublishPlan`, and every nested payload type (`CratePublish`, `NpmPublish`, `NpmMainPublish`, `PypiPublish`, `ReleaseEntry`) carry `deny_unknown_fields`, so a field present in the received bytes but unknown to this build is a hard deserialization failure rather than a silent drop -- none of these types carries that attribute at last_verified_revision. Both digests are SHA-256 over a canonical encoding in which object keys are sorted lexicographically by Unicode scalar value at every nesting level, there is no insignificant whitespace, and a field whose value is absent (Rust `None`, or an empty `Vec` under `skip_serializing_if`) is omitted from the canonical form identically to a field that was never present in the source data -- the canonicalizer never emits an explicit null. Neither digest is computed over the envelope or any of its own fields, so the scheme is free of self-reference.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-002",
      "criterion": "`configDigest` is SHA-256 over the canonical encoding of the object `{\"files\": [...]}`, where the array is ordered by `path` sorted lexicographically by Unicode scalar value, every `path` is workspace-root-relative using `/` separators, and each element is either `{\"path\": <path>, \"sha256\": <64 lowercase hex of the file's raw bytes>}` or `{\"path\": <path>, \"absent\": true}`. The path set is exactly and exhaustively: (1) `callisto.toml`; (2) `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; (3) `Cargo.toml`; (4) `package.json`; (5) `pyproject.toml`; (6) `.changeset/pre.json`; (7) `<changesets_dir>/pre.json` when the resolved `[changesets].dir` differs from `.changeset`; and (8) every file matching `<changesets_dir>/*.md` in a single non-recursive directory read, excluding exactly the name `README.md`. `<changesets_dir>` is the resolved `[changesets].dir` from `callisto.toml`, defaulting to `.changeset` (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:248-262). Entries (1) through (7) are a fixed list independent of what exists on disk: each one that is absent contributes an `absent: true` element, never a hard error, because every one of them is legitimately optional at run time -- `config::load` falls back to `RawConfig::default()` when `callisto.toml` is missing (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:231-244) and the membership readers treat a missing root manifest as admit-all (crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs). Entry (8) is an enumeration, so an absent or empty directory contributes no elements. A file that exists but whose bytes cannot be read -- a permission error, an I/O error, or a symlink loop -- is a hard error that terminates digest computation with a non-zero exit; it MUST NOT be recorded as absent, because absent and unreadable are distinct facts and conflating them would let a permissions change pass validation silently. Root `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, and `pyproject.toml` appear here because their workspace-membership tables govern package discovery; their per-package content also reaches `inputDigest` through resolved state, and that redundancy is intentional.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "`inputDigest` is SHA-256 over the canonical encoding of the object `{\"packages\": [...]}`, where the array is sorted lexicographically by Unicode scalar value of each element's serialized `packageId`, and each element carries exactly these fields: `packageId` (the JSON form of `callisto_model::PackageId`); `manifestPaths` (workspace-root-relative manifest paths for that package, lexicographically sorted); `currentVersion` (the rendered `Version`, omitted when unknown); `publishTo` (rendered `PublishTarget` strings, lexicographically sorted); `dependencies` (sorted by `name` then `kind`, each `{\"name\", \"kind\", \"spec\"}` with `spec` omitted when none); `changelogPath` (workspace-root-relative, omitted when the package has none); and `role` (the rendered `ManifestRole`). This is exactly the manifest-derived state `plan_publish` consumes: identity and version from `Cargo.toml` `package.name`/`package.version`, `package.json` `name`/`version`, and `pyproject.toml` `project.name`/`project.version` with the poetry and flit fallbacks; `publishTo` from `Cargo.toml` `package.publish`, `package.json` `private`/`publishConfig`, and any `callisto.toml` `[[package]]`/`[[package-set]]` `publish-to` override (crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:306-399); dependency edges, which determine `publish_order`; the changelog path, which determines `ReleaseEntry.changelogSection`; and the role, which classifies npm platform versus main packages. Lockfiles are excluded because no lockfile content is read during planning -- `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, and `package-lock.json` are only stat'd for existence (crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:421-443) and `Cargo.lock`, `uv.lock`, and `poetry.lock` are untouched until apply (crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:418-428). Git tag state is excluded because tag creation is an effect of executing this very plan, so hashing it would make a plan invalidate itself mid-execution; the commit the plan was made against is bound by `sourceCommit` instead. Because `inputDigest` is computed over resolved discovery output rather than over a file list, inputs that only influence which packages are discovered -- in-tree `.gitignore` files, honored by `WalkBuilder::git_ignore(true)` at crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs:42-43 -- are covered transitively by their effect on the package set.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004",
      "criterion": "This build accepts exactly `schemaVersion = 1` on the envelope, `digestSchemeVersion = 1`, and a payload `plan.schemaVersion` equal to `callisto_model::SCHEMA_VERSION` (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:12, currently `1`). Any other value in any of those three fields -- higher, lower, non-integer, or absent -- terminates with a non-zero exit before any digest is recomputed and before any mutation is attempted. There is no compatibility shim, no field back-filling, and no best-effort acceptance of a lower version. The diagnostic carries exactly these fields: `field` (which of the three), `found` (the value read, or the literal `absent`), `supported` (the single value this build accepts), and `source` (the plan's origin -- the file path, or `-` for stdin).",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-005",
      "criterion": "The canonical encoder rejects any floating-point value (`f32` or `f64`) encountered while serializing the envelope, terminating digest computation with a non-zero exit and a diagnostic naming the JSON pointer of the offending value and the Rust type and field it came from. No envelope or payload type contains a floating-point field at last_verified_revision (verified across `PublishPlanEnvelope`, `PublishPlan`, `CratePublish`, `NpmPublish`, `NpmMainPublish`, `PypiPublish`, `ReleaseEntry`, and `NpmAccess`), so this path is unreachable today; the criterion exists so that introducing a float is a hard, immediate failure at digest time rather than a silent cross-platform digest divergence, and so no float-formatting standard needs to be specified for a case that cannot occur. A test asserts that canonicalizing a wrapper struct containing an `f64` returns an error rather than any encoded output.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-006",
      "criterion": "Envelope validation is a total, fail-closed check that is STRUCTURAL with respect to the operation set and observation-driven only with respect to disk-state digests. Concretely: the envelope bytes are deserialized under the `deny_unknown_fields` types of AC-001 and re-serialized under AC-001's canonical encoding; `configDigest` and `inputDigest` are recomputed from currently observed disk state per AC-002 and AC-003 and compared for exact string equality against the envelope's values; `sourceCommit` is compared for exact equality against the git HEAD SHA observed at validation time; and `schemaVersion`, `digestSchemeVersion`, and payload `plan.schemaVersion` are checked per AC-004. The requested operation set -- every entry of `rustCrates`, `npmPlatformPackages`, `npmMainPackages`, `pypiPackages`, and `releases` -- is taken verbatim from the envelope and MUST NOT be independently re-derived, re-observed, or regenerated by a fresh planning pass; a test asserts the validation path invokes neither `callisto_graph::commands::plan_publish` nor `callisto_graph::commands::version::plan_version`. Recomputing the digests is observation of config and manifest state, which is precisely what those digests exist to bind; it is not observation of what should be published, and this distinction is what makes AC-006 compatible with SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001B's rule that plan-driven execution never recomputes a plan for itself. `generatedAt` is recorded for audit and is not compared. `PublishPlan::diagnostics` (crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:39) does not participate in the comparison: it is informational human-readable output, not part of the operation set being validated, and it is excluded from `inputDigest` for the same reason. For the fields that do participate, an omitted array and an explicit empty array are equal, not a mismatch -- `pypiPackages` carries `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Vec::is_empty\")]`, so both forms deserialize to the same value and both re-serialize to omission -- and a test asserts a plan with `pypiPackages` omitted and one with `pypiPackages: []` produce byte-identical canonical encodings and equal digests. That equivalence is the only defaulting permitted for a participating field: any new participating field whose serde default is not identical to its canonical-omission form MUST be introduced together with a `schemaVersion` increment. Validation fails closed -- any error while recomputing current state (a present-but-unreadable file, an unparseable manifest, an unavailable git HEAD, a digest computation failure) is treated as a mismatch and blocks the consumer, never as a pass. On any mismatch the diagnostic identifies every mismatching or unrecomputable field, not just the first one found.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-007",
      "criterion": "The envelope is structurally guaranteed to be secret-free by construction. A module `crates/callisto-model/src/plan_provenance.rs` declares `pub enum FieldSource { Manifest, CallistoConfig, GitRef, ComputedVersion, Constant }` -- an enumeration with no variant that can denote a process environment variable, a CLI credential flag, or any value flowing through the registry-authentication path, so an environment-sourced field is unrepresentable in the provenance table -- and `pub const PLAN_FIELD_PROVENANCE: &[(&str, &str, FieldSource)]` holding one `(type_name, serialized_field_name, source)` triple per field, with `serialized_field_name` in the camelCase form the type actually serializes. A test generates `schemars::schema_for!(PublishPlanEnvelope)` -- `schemars` is already a dependency of `callisto-model` (crates/callisto-model/Cargo.toml:28) and every type below already derives `JsonSchema` -- walks the generated schema's definitions for `PublishPlanEnvelope`, `PublishPlan`, `CratePublish`, `NpmPublish`, `NpmMainPublish`, `PypiPublish`, `ReleaseEntry`, and `NpmAccess`, and asserts both directions: every `(type, field)` in the generated schema has exactly one entry in `PLAN_FIELD_PROVENANCE`, and every entry in `PLAN_FIELD_PROVENANCE` names a field present in the generated schema. Adding a field without a provenance entry fails the first assertion; removing a field without removing its entry fails the second. The test lives in `callisto-model` alone, because every envelope and payload type lives in that crate and `VersionPlan` is excluded from the envelope per this spec's non_goals.",
      "is_error_case": true
    }
  ],
  "implementation_notes": [
    "Canonicalization (AC-001): `olpc-cjson` is a `serde_json::Formatter` already used in production by AWS's `tough` (TUF) crate, and is already present in Cargo.lock at 0.1.4 as a transitive dependency of `oci-client`. Apply it directly against the typed structs via `serde_json::Serializer::with_formatter`, avoiding an intermediate `serde_json::Value` and this workspace's `preserve_order` serde_json feature (which makes `Value` insertion-ordered, not sorted). `serde_json_canonicalizer` (strict RFC 8785 JCS) is a stricter but less production-proven alternative.",
    "Float rejection (AC-005): olpc-cjson's canonical-JSON dialect has no float representation. If its `Formatter` implementation does not itself return an error from `write_f32`/`write_f64`, wrap it in a newtype `Formatter` that overrides both to return `io::Error` -- do not rely on the underlying crate's behavior without a test pinning it, since a silent fallback to `serde_json`'s default float formatting is exactly the cross-platform digest divergence AC-005 exists to prevent.",
    "Hashing (AC-002, AC-003): `sha2` is present in Cargo.lock at both 0.10.9 and 0.11.0 but is not a direct dependency of any workspace crate. Add `sha2 = \"0.11\"` to `callisto-model` explicitly rather than relying on the transitive pin.",
    "Omitted-vs-null (AC-001): a `#[serde(skip_serializing_if)]`-skipped field is invisible to any serde-Formatter-based canonicalizer by construction, satisfying 'omitted == never present' automatically. `PublishPlan::pypi_packages` and `PublishPlan::diagnostics` already carry `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Vec::is_empty\")]` (crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:33,38), so this path is live today. It does not by itself guarantee 'omitted == explicit null' -- that holds only as long as no field's `Option<T>` can serialize `Some(Value::Null)`. Worth a one-line comment at the point of digest computation.",
    "deny_unknown_fields (AC-001): adding this attribute to `PublishPlan` and its nested types is a behavior change for the existing `callisto tag --plan` and `callisto filter-plan --plan` inputs (crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs:224,240), which today silently ignore unknown keys. That tightening is intended and in scope.",
    "Config input set (AC-002): `callisto.toml` is the single configuration file, resolved as one `root.join(\"callisto.toml\")` with no ancestor walk, no layering, no `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` path, and no per-package config file -- per-package setti…273 tokens truncated…arget`, `node_modules`, `.git`, `.moon`, `dist` (crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/ignore_walk.rs:18-146). No other manifest kind is enumerated.",
    "Provenance table (AC-007): making the third tuple element a closed `FieldSource` enum rather than a free-form `&str` accessor description is what turns AC-007 from a documentation convention into a type-level guarantee -- a string description could name `std::env::var` and only a substring check would catch it, whereas the enum has no variant capable of expressing it."
  ]
}
{
  "id": "SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002",
  "status": "proposed",
  "owner_track": "release-security",
  "last_verified_revision": "59023bd3286650394af37bc34bd688b51dba3d92",
  "depends_on": ["SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A"],
  "purpose": "Bind release intent, release tags, and publish reports to one immutable source commit, and give that binding an enforceable policy surface with a named consumer and a stated failure behavior, while keeping the core release engine independent of GitHub or any particular signing service.",
  "scope": "Source-commit resolution and validation rules layered on top of the plan-level `source_commit` field mandated by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A AC-001; per-package `ReleaseEntry.sha` consistency with that field; commit and tag resolution before mutation; a provider-neutral provenance policy with an explicit enforcement point in the tag and publish paths; clear diagnostics for mismatch. Forge-specific authorization and attestation integration are adapters. Note on the AC-002 HEAD == source_commit check: SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A owns, as its committed primary architecture, the split of release work into an unprivileged planning job and a separate privileged execution job (the split SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003 AC-001 configures for GitHub Actions). Because the plan crosses a job boundary by design, the executing job re-checks out the repository independently of the planning job, and the AC-002 check is load-bearing from the first implementation -- not a conditional requirement awaiting an uncertain architecture decision, and not the near-tautology it would be inside a single checkout. The executing job must consume a pinned-SHA checkout of `source_commit`, never a floating branch or symbolic ref; AC-002 is what detects a violation of that rule.",
  "non_goals": [
    "Mandating GPG, SSH, Sigstore, GitHub, GitLab, Bazel, or any other forge or signing provider.",
    "Claiming that a Git SHA is a cryptographic author signature.",
    "Changing a pre-existing tag to force it onto a requested commit.",
    "Implementing a concrete signature or attestation verifier. This spec requires the policy type, its placement in configuration and in the plan envelope, its enforcement point before mutation, and its failure behavior; producing `VerificationEvidence` for any specific provider is an adapter's job and is out of scope here. What is explicitly NOT permitted is satisfying this spec with a serializable-but-unconsumed policy type: a `ProvenancePolicy` that no code reads at an enforcement point does not satisfy AC-004 or AC-005."
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-001",
      "criterion": "This spec does not introduce the plan-level `source_commit` field -- that field is defined by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A AC-001, which mandates it on the plan envelope. This spec adds resolution and validation rules on top of that field: `source_commit` is resolved from Git at planning time and is never inferred from a branch name during execution; every generated VersionPlan, PublishPlan, tag report, and publish report carries the full resolved SHA (not a shortened form) via that field. Additionally, for every `ReleaseEntry` in a plan, its existing `sha: CommitSha` field (crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:130) must equal the plan-level `source_commit`; plan validation rejects a plan where any entry's `sha` diverges from the plan-level `source_commit`, reporting the entry's package id, its sha, and the plan's source_commit in the diagnostic.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-002",
      "criterion": "Before any apply, tag, or publish mutation, execution resolves HEAD and requires it to equal the plan's `source_commit`. A detached HEAD is permitted when it matches; a branch name, shallow symbolic reference, or changed worktree cannot substitute for equality. The comparison is an exact, full-length, case-normalized (lowercase hex) comparison of the complete SHA -- a prefix or short-SHA match is never treated as equality, even when the prefix is unambiguous, to prevent a false pass on hash-prefix coincidence. Both sides of the comparison are `CommitSha` values (crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs:296), whose `parse` constructor already enforces exactly 40 ASCII hex digits and lowercases them, so full-length and case normalization are type-level guarantees rather than call-site discipline; a raw `&str` comparison that bypasses `CommitSha` does not satisfy this criterion. On mismatch, execution fails before any mutation and reports a stable, structured error type/variant (not free-text-only diagnostic text) carrying both the resolved HEAD SHA and the plan's source_commit, so calling code -- including the GitHub Actions adapter per SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003 AC-006 -- can match on the error type programmatically without string-parsing.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "A newly created release tag is an annotated tag (`git tag -a`, i.e. a Git tag object, not a lightweight ref) created at the exact source commit SHA and carrying that SHA as its target. When an expected tag already exists, resolution reads the tag object and peels it to its target commit, and the idempotent-match-versus-conflict decision is made against that peeled commit -- a lightweight ref or a tag object peeling to a different commit is a conflict, never a silent match. This is a new invariant layered on top of the already-shipped idempotency behavior of `CreatedTag` (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:611): the existing `sha` and `already_existed` fields, and the existing idempotent-match-vs-conflict semantics documented at docs/01-spec.md §M.12.6, are unchanged by this spec and are not re-specified here.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004",
      "criterion": "The documented baseline policy is SHA-anchored provenance: plans, tags, artifacts, and reports identify the same immutable commit. Documentation explicitly says this binds state but does not prove human authorship. The core model (crates/callisto-model) defines two serializable types with no forge-SDK dependency: `ProvenancePolicy { mode: ProvenanceMode, trust_roots: Vec<TrustRootRef>, failure: ProvenanceFailure }`, where `ProvenanceMode` is `ShaOnly | RequireVerifiedEvidence`, `TrustRootRef` is an opaque provider-defined identifier, and `ProvenanceFailure` is `RejectBeforeMutation`; and `VerificationEvidence { verifier, issuer, subject, verified_at, source_commit: CommitSha }`. The policy has a required placement, not merely a representable shape: it is resolved from workspace configuration through the existing raw-to-resolved config pipeline (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/raw.rs and resolve.rs), defaulting to `ShaOnly` when unconfigured, and the resolved policy is carried on the plan envelope so planning and execution agree on one policy value. Its named consumers are `TagReport` and `PublishReport` (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:589 and :40), each of which records the effective `ProvenancePolicy` and any `VerificationEvidence` that was accepted, so a report reader can audit which policy was in force and what satisfied it without a forge-specific integration.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-005",
      "criterion": "Provider adapters supply attestations or signature-verification evidence, but their absence cannot cause the core domain crates to depend on a forge SDK. Enforcement is explicit and happens in core, before mutation: when the effective `ProvenancePolicy.mode` is `RequireVerifiedEvidence`, execution requires, before any tag, publish, or release mutation, at least one `VerificationEvidence` whose `source_commit` equals the plan's `source_commit` under the same exact full-length lowercase-hex comparison as AC-002, and whose verifier or issuer matches every configured `TrustRootRef`; if evidence is absent, binds to a different commit, or satisfies no configured trust root, execution fails with a structured error variant naming which condition failed and performs no mutation (`ProvenanceFailure::RejectBeforeMutation`). When `mode` is `ShaOnly`, absent evidence is permitted and is not an error, and any evidence that is present is still recorded on the report. Core validates evidence shape and its binding to `source_commit`; it does not perform cryptographic verification itself, which is the adapter's responsibility. A test asserts the enforcement point directly: with `mode: RequireVerifiedEvidence` and no evidence, the tag and publish paths return the error variant and no mutation is observable.",
      "is_error_case": true
    }
  ],
  "implementation_notes": [
    "gix (crates/callisto-vcs/Cargo.toml:21, gix = \"0.86\") reads a commit's raw signature header (`gpgsig`) but does not verify it -- confirmed still true at the version in use. Any adapter implementing AC-004/AC-005 needs a separate verification path; gix alone is insufficient.",
    "For a GitHub adapter specifically: GitHub already computes and exposes `verification.verified`/`verification.reason` per commit via its REST/GraphQL API. Shelling to `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}` (consistent with this repo's existing `gh`-shelling pattern in .github/actions/callisto-action) is sufficient to populate `VerificationEvidence` for that adapter and needs no signature-verification crate at all.",
    "For a non-GitHub or independent-verification adapter: `sequoia-openpgp` (actively maintained, reached 1.0) for GPG; `ssh-key` crate (feature-gated per-algorithm) or shelling to `ssh-keygen -Y verify` for SSH signatures -- the latter avoids a new dependency entirely, consistent with this repo's existing subprocess-shelling conventions; `sigstore` crate for keyless/Sigstore attestation, noting it is pre-1.0 and should be pinned tightly if adopted. None of these are needed for this spec itself, whose core requirement is the policy, its placement, and its enforcement point -- they matter only when a concrete evidence-producing adapter is built.",
    "Placement (AC-004): the policy types belong in callisto-model, which is a Layer 1 crate under the workspace's permissive-license and no-AGPL-dependency invariant (CLAUDE.md); serde and schemars are already available there, and neither `ProvenancePolicy` nor `VerificationEvidence` pulls in a forge SDK. Config resolution follows the established `RawXConfig` -> `ResolvedConfig` pairing in crates/callisto-graph/src/config/.",
    "Sequencing (AC-002): `source_commit` does not yet exist anywhere in the workspace -- confirmed by grep at the revision recorded in last_verified_revision. It arrives with SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A AC-001, which is why that spec is this spec's declared depends_on. The current .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml has a `verify` job and a single `release` job that plans and executes in one shell sequence, with no `environment:` key; the planning/execution split that makes AC-002 non-tautological lands with SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A and is configured for GitHub by SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003 AC-001."
  ]
}

  "id": "SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003",

Note on the AC-002 HEAD == source_commit check: SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A owns, as its committed primary architecture, the split of release work into an unprivileged planning job and a separate privileged execution job (the split SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003 AC-001 configures for GitHub Actions). Because the plan crosses a job boundary by design, the executing job re-checks out the repository independently of the planning job, and the AC-002 check is load-bearing from the first implementation -- not a conditional requirement awaiting an uncertain architecture decision, and not the near-tautology it would be inside a single checkout.   "non_goals": [
    "Mandating GPG, SSH, Sigstore, GitHub, GitLab, Bazel, or any other forge or signing provider.",
    "Claiming that a Git SHA is a cryptographic author signature.",
    "Changing a pre-existing tag to force it onto a requested commit.",
    "Implementing a concrete signature or attestation verifier. This spec requires the policy type, its placement in configuration and in the plan envelope, its enforcement point before mutation, and its failure behavior; producing `VerificationEvidence` for any specific provider is an adapter's job and is out of scope here. What is explicitly NOT permitted is satisfying this spec with a serializable-but-unconsumed policy type: a `ProvenancePolicy` that no code reads at an enforcement point does not satisfy AC-004 or AC-005."
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-001",
      "criterion": "This spec does not introduce the plan-level `source_commit` field -- that field is defined by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A AC-001, which mandates it on the plan envelope. This spec adds resolution and validation rules on top of that field: `source_commit` is resolved from Git at planning time and is never inferred from a branch name during execution; every generated VersionPlan, PublishPlan, tag report, and publish report carries the full resolved SHA (not a shortened form) via that field. Additionally, for every `ReleaseEntry` in a plan, its existing `sha: CommitSha` field (crates/callisto-model/src/plan.rs:130) must equal the plan-level `source_commit`; plan validation rejects a plan where any entry's `sha` diverges from the plan-level `source_commit`, reporting the entry's package id, its sha, and the plan's source_commit in the diagnostic.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-002",
      "criterion": "Before any apply, tag, or publish mutation, execution resolves HEAD and requires it to equal the plan's `source_commit`. A detached HEAD is permitted when it matches; a branch name, shallow symbolic reference, or changed worktree cannot substitute for equality. The comparison is an exact, full-length, case-normalized (lowercase hex) comparison of the complete SHA -- a prefix or short-SHA match is never treated as equality, even when the prefix is unambiguous, to prevent a false pass on hash-prefix coincidence. Both sides of the comparison are `CommitSha` values (crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs:296), whose `parse` constructor already enforces exactly 40 ASCII hex digits and lowercases them, so full-length and case normalization are type-level guarantees rather than call-site discipline; a raw `&str` comparison that bypasses `CommitSha` does not satisfy this criterion. On mismatch, execution fails before any mutation and reports a stable, structured error type/variant (not free-text-only diagnostic text) carrying both the resolved HEAD SHA and the plan's source_commit, so calling code -- including the GitHub Actions adapter per SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003 AC-006 -- can match on the error type programmatically without string-parsing.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "A newly created release tag is an annotated tag (`git tag -a`, i.e. a Git tag object, not a lightweight ref) created at the exact source commit SHA and carrying that SHA as its target. When an expected tag already exists, resolution reads the tag object and peels it to its target commit, and the idempotent-match-versus-conflict decision is made against that peeled commit -- a lightweight ref or a tag object peeling to a different commit is a conflict, never a silent match. This is a new invariant layered on top of the already-shipped idempotency behavior of `CreatedTag` (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:611): the existing `sha` and `already_existed` fields, and the existing idempotent-match-vs-conflict semantics documented at docs/01-spec.md §M.12.6, are unchanged by this spec and are not re-specified here.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004",
      "criterion": "The documented baseline policy is SHA-anchored provenance: plans, tags, artifacts, and reports identify the same immutable commit. Documentation explicitly says this binds state but does not prove human authorship. The core model (crates/callisto-model) defines two serializable types with no forge-SDK dependency: `ProvenancePolicy { mode: ProvenanceMode, trust_roots: Vec<TrustRootRef>, failure: ProvenanceFailure }`, where `ProvenanceMode` is `ShaOnly | RequireVerifiedEvidence`, `TrustRootRef` is an opaque provider-defined identifier, and `ProvenanceFailure` is `RejectBeforeMutation`; and `VerificationEvidence { verifier, issuer, subject, verified_at, source_commit: CommitSha }`. The policy has a required placement, not merely a representable shape: it is resolved from workspace configuration through the existing raw-to-resolved config pipeline (crates/callisto-graph/src/config/raw.rs and resolve.rs), defaulting to `ShaOnly` when unconfigured, and the resolved policy is carried on the plan envelope so planning and execution agree on one policy value. Its named consumers are `TagReport` and `PublishReport` (crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs:589 and :40), each of which records the effective `ProvenancePolicy` and any `VerificationEvidence` that was accepted, so a report reader can audit which policy was in force and what satisfied it without a forge-specific integration.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-005",
      "criterion": "Provider adapters supply attestations or signature-verification evidence, but their absence cannot cause the core domain crates to depend on a forge SDK. Enforcement is explicit and happens in core, before mutation: when the effective `ProvenancePolicy.mode` is `RequireVerifiedEvidence`, execution requires, before any tag, publish, or release mutation, at least one `VerificationEvidence` whose `source_commit` equals the plan's `source_commit` under the same exact full-length lowercase-hex comparison as AC-002, and whose verifier or issuer matches every configured `TrustRootRef`; if evidence is absent, binds to a different commit, or satisfies no configured trust root, execution fails with a structured error variant naming which condition failed and performs no mutation (`ProvenanceFailure::RejectBeforeMutation`). When `mode` is `ShaOnly`, absent evidence is permitted and is not an error, and any evidence that is present is still recorded on the report. Core validates evidence shape and its binding to `source_commit`; it does not perform cryptographic verification itself, which is the adapter's responsibility. A test asserts the enforcement point directly: with `mode: RequireVerifiedEvidence` and no evidence, the tag and publish paths return the error variant and no mutation is observable.",
      "is_error_case": true
    }
  ],
  "implementation_notes": [
    "gix (crates/callisto-vcs/Cargo.toml:21, gix = \"0.86\") reads a commit's raw signature header (`gpgsig`) but does not verify it -- confirmed still true at the version in use. Any adapter implementing AC-004/AC-005 needs a separate verification path; gix alone is insufficient.",
    "For a GitHub adapter specifically: GitHub already computes and exposes `verification.verified`/`verification.reason` per commit via its REST/GraphQL API. Shelling to `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}` (consistent with this repo's existing `gh`-shelling pattern in .github/actions/callisto-action) is sufficient to populate `VerificationEvidence` for that adapter and needs no signature-verification crate at all.",
    "For a non-GitHub or independent-verification adapter: `sequoia-openpgp` (actively maintained, reached 1.0) for GPG; `ssh-key` crate (feature-gated per-algorithm) or shelling to `ssh-keygen -Y verify` for SSH signatures -- the latter avoids a new dependency entirely, consistent with this repo's existing subprocess-shelling conventions; `sigstore` crate for keyless/Sigstore attestation, noting it is pre-1.0 and should be pinned tightly if adopted. None of these are needed for this spec itself, whose core requirement is the policy, its placement, and its enforcement point -- they matter only when a concrete evidence-producing adapter is built.",
    "Placement (AC-004): the policy types belong in callisto-model, which is a Layer 1 crate under the workspace's permissive-license and no-AGPL-dependency invariant (CLAUDE.md); serde and schemars are already available there, and neither `ProvenancePolicy` nor `VerificationEvidence` pulls in a forge SDK.     "Sequencing (AC-002): `source_commit` does not yet exist anywhere in the workspace -- confirmed by grep at the revision recorded in last_verified_revision. It arrives with SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A AC-001, which is why that spec is this spec's declared depends_on. The current .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml has a `verify` job and a single `release` job that plans and executes in one shell sequence, with no `environment:` key; the planning/execution split that makes AC-002 non-tautological lands with SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A and is configured for GitHub by SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003 AC-001."
  ]
}
{
  "id": "SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003",
  "status": "proposed",
  "owner_track": "release-security",
  "last_verified_revision": "59023bd3286650394af37bc34bd688b51dba3d92",
  "depends_on": [
    "SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A",
    "SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001B",
    "SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C",
    "SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002"
  ],
  "purpose": "Harden the GitHub Actions release adapter so registry publication and repository mutation occur only through a narrowly authorized, reviewable release boundary.",
  "scope": ".github/workflows/callisto-release.yml and its referenced actions, GitHub Environment configuration documentation, action pinning, permissions, artifact handoff, and workflow tests. The non_goal below of not making GitHub Actions the only supported CI/release platform refers to the portability of the callisto CLI as a build tool; it does not constrain the mechanisms this repository's own meta-release pipeline may use. A GitHub-Environment-specific protection gate on this repo's release workflow (AC-001) is in scope and does not conflict with that non-goal. This spec declares its build dependencies explicitly in depends_on. SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A defines the durable-plan envelope schema; SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001B defines the CLI command-mode separation and operation-status record; SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C owns the plan-job to execute-job topology and the artifact upload/download flow. None of the three exists in the current workflow, where a single `release` job invokes the composite callisto-action and computes the plan inline (`callisto plan-publish`) in the same shell block that pushes tags and creates the GitHub release. AC-001 and AC-006 consume that topology and that envelope rather than defining them, and must therefore be sequenced after all three ship. SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002 owns source_commit resolution and the structured HEAD-vs-source_commit mismatch error that AC-006's validation step matches on.",
  "non_goals": [
    "Making GitHub Actions the only supported CI or release platform.",
    "Moving provider-neutral release rules from callisto core into workflow shell code.",
    "Requiring Git tag signing in this track; signature policy is covered by SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002.",
    "Defining the plan/execute job topology or the durable-plan envelope schema. Those are owned by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A/001B/001C; this spec consumes them and adds the authorization, pinning, permission, and review boundary around the execute job."
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    {
      "id": "AC-001",
      "criterion": "The workflow's current single `release` job (which today computes the plan and performs tag/publish/gh-release in one shell script) is split into two jobs per the plan-job to execute-job topology defined by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C: an unprivileged planning job with no registry secrets and a read-only or no GITHUB_TOKEN, and a separate privileged execution job that performs tag/publish/release actions. The execution job is bound to a GitHub Environment (`environment:` key referencing a named environment such as `release`) that has required reviewers and branch/tag deployment rules configured. The repository documents that environment's name, its required reviewers, its branch/tag deployment rules, and an administrator-verifiable API or console procedure for confirming those rules are actually configured on the repository. The workflow YAML `environment:` reference alone is explicitly insufficient evidence that protection rules exist: the key declares intent, and GitHub auto-creates a referenced environment with zero protection rules on first use unless required reviewers have been separately configured via repo Settings. This criterion owns the topology and the documented procedure; AC-004 owns the automated enforcement that the documented rules are live. Non-release jobs (verify, planning) receive neither registry secrets nor write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN permissions.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-002",
      "criterion": "Each workflow and job declares the least GitHub token permissions it needs. contents, pull-requests, checks, and statuses are write-scoped only in the job that demonstrably performs that operation; all other jobs default to read or none. A workflow test or policy check rejects an unscoped top-level write grant.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to immutable full commit SHAs (40 hex characters), each with a nearby comment recording the upstream tag or release used, for human review.",
      "is_error_case": false
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004b",
      "criterion": "CI verifies every external action reference's pin format and fails the build if any external action reference is changed to a mutable tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-004",
      "criterion": "A CI or setup check calls the GitHub API (e.g. `gh api repos/{repo}/environments/{name}`) against the environment named in AC-001's `environment:` key and fails unless that environment's `protection_rules` array contains an entry with `\"type\": \"required_reviewers\"` and a non-empty `reviewers` list. A non-empty `protection_rules` array is not by itself sufficient: live GitHub data confirms environments commonly carry only a `branch_policy` rule (restricts which branch may deploy) with no human approval gate at all -- that shape must still fail this check. This check is the automated enforcement of AC-001's evidentiary rule, and it must read live environment configuration through the API rather than inspecting workflow YAML, so that a diff which merely adds `environment: release` can never by itself satisfy it.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-006",
      "criterion": "The planning job (per AC-001) uploads the explicit durable plan defined by SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A as a build artifact per SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001C's upload/download flow. The privileged execution job downloads only that artifact from its own workflow run, verifies its source_commit against its own checkout per SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002 AC-002, and fails before any registry or repository credentials are used if validation fails, surfacing that spec's structured mismatch error rather than a free-text-only diagnostic. Caches may accelerate dependency installation but are never read as release intent. Implementation of this criterion is blocked on SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A/001B/001C shipping the envelope schema, command-mode separation, and artifact upload/download flow first; see depends_on and the scope note on sequencing.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-007",
      "criterion": "Changes to files under `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/` require review from a designated set of owners before merge, enforced via CODEOWNERS combined with a branch protection rule requiring that review on those paths. This is distinct from and in addition to AC-001's environment gate: the environment gate controls who can trigger a *deployment* from an already-merged workflow, while this criterion controls who can *merge changes* to the workflow/action definitions that determine what a future deployment does.",
      "is_error_case": true
    }
  ],
  "implementation_notes": [
    "AC-004b (SHA-pin drift detection): consider adopting the maintained `step-security/github-actions-ensure-sha-pinned-actions` GitHub Action rather than hand-rolling the check -- it is the actively maintained successor to the now-stale `zgosalvez/github-actions-ensure-sha-pinned-actions`. Whichever is adopted must itself be pinned to a commit SHA, or it reintroduces the exact circular-trust problem AC-003 targets.",
    "AC-003/AC-004b/AC-004 are pure GitHub Actions YAML/CLI concerns -- stay with `gh api` and shell, consistent with callisto-action's existing pattern (action.yml already shells to `gh` for every GitHub interaction). No Rust crate (e.g. octocrab) is warranted for this narrow, workflow-scoped check."
  ]
}

/// Arguments for the `plan-publish` command.
#[derive(Args, Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PlanPublishArgs {
    /// Plan only the named package(s). Repeatable: `--package foo --package bar`.
    #[arg(long = "package", value_name = "NAME")]
    pub only: Vec<String>,
}

/// Arguments for the `publish` command.
#[derive(Args, Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PublishArgs {
    /// Publish only the named package(s). Repeatable: `--package foo --package bar`.
    /// When omitted, all packages in the plan are published.
    #[arg(long = "package", value_name = "NAME")]
    pub only: Vec<String>,
    /// Skip the pre-publish "already published?" registry check and publish
    /// directly, relying on the registry's own already-published response.
    /// Saves one round-trip per package, at the cost of re-running local
    /// publish lifecycle scripts (e.g. npm's prepublishOnly) on a retried
    /// publish of an already-published version.
    #[arg(long)]
    pub skip_publish_precheck: bool,
}

/// Arguments for the `compose-pr-body` command.
#[derive(Args, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ComposePrBodyArgs {
    /// Existing PR body text to merge with, or `-` to read it from stdin.
    #[arg(long, value_name = "TEXT|-")]
    pub existing_body: Option<String>,
    /// Label to attach to the PR body; repeatable.
    #[arg(long = "label")]
    pub labels: Vec<String>,
    /// Branch name to reference in the generated PR body.
    #[arg(long)]
    pub branch: Option<String>,
}

/// Arguments for the `tag` command.
#[derive(Args, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TagArgs {
    /// Path to a publish plan JSON file, inline JSON, or `-` to read it from stdin.
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE|-")]
    pub plan: String,
    /// Also move a floating major-version tag (e.g. `v1`) to point at the new tag.
    #[arg(long)]
    pub floating_major: bool,
    /// Abort if the workspace graph contains crosscheck failures or other
    /// error-severity diagnostics.
    #[arg(long)]
    pub strict: bool,
}

/// Arguments for the `filter-plan` command.
#[derive(Args, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct FilterPlanArgs {
    /// Path to a publish plan JSON file, inline JSON, or `-` to read it from stdin.
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE|-")]
    pub plan: String,
    /// Path to a publish report JSON file, inline JSON, or `-` to read it from stdin.
    #[arg(long, value_name = "FILE|-")]
    pub report: String,
}

/// Arguments for the `completions` command.
#[derive(Args, Clone, Debug)]
pub struct CompletionsArgs {
    /// Shell to generate a completion script for.
    #[arg(value_enum)]
    pub shell: clap_complete::Shell,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use clap::CommandFactory;

    /// QW-5: --strict flag on status subcommand must have a meaningful help string.
    #[test]
    fn strict_flag_help_text_is_meaningful() {
        let mut cmd = Cli::command();
        cmd.build();

        // Find the "status" subcommand.
        let status_sub = cmd
            .get_subcommands()
            .find(|s| s.get_name() == "status")
            .expect("status subcommand must exist");

        // Find the --strict argument.
        let strict_arg = status_sub
            .get_arguments()
            .find(|a| a.get_long() == Some("strict"))
            .expect("--strict argument must exist on status subcommand");

        let help = strict_arg
            .get_help()
            .map(|h| h.to_string())
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .to_lowercase();

        // Must contain "strict" and describe what it does.
        assert!(
            help.contains("strict"),
            "--strict help text must contain the word 'strict'; got: {help:?}"
        );
        assert!(
            help.contains("warning") || help.contains("error"),
            "--strict help text must mention 'warning' or 'error'; got: {help:?}"
        );
        // Must be longer than a placeholder.
        assert!(
            help.len() > 20,
            "--strict help text is too short to be meaningful: {help:?}"
        );
    }

    /// AC-006/AC-007 (parse slice): `callisto matrix --package foo` parses
    /// into Command::Matrix with the package field populated; MatrixArgs
    /// declares no --format of its own (the global flag is used instead).
    #[test]
    fn test_cli_parse_matrix_command_with_package() {
        use clap::Parser;
        let cli = Cli::parse_from(["callisto", "matrix", "--package", "foo"]);
        if let Command::Matrix(args) = cli.command {
            assert_eq!(args.package, Some("foo".to_string()));
        } else {
            panic!("Expected Matrix command");
        }
    }

    /// AC-003b: bare `callisto matrix` (no --package) parses with package: None.
    #[test]
    fn test_cli_parse_matrix_command_bare() {
        use clap::Parser;
        let cli = Cli::parse_from(["callisto", "matrix"]);
        if let Command::Matrix(args) = cli.command {
            assert_eq!(args.package, None);
        } else {
            panic!("Expected Matrix command");
        }
    }
}
name: 'Callisto Release Action'
description: 'Automated changesets release manager: creates version PRs or publishes packages'
inputs:
  publish:
    description: 'Command to run when publishing packages (e.g. "moon run :publish", "cargo publish", or "pnpm publish")'
    required: false
  version_command:
    description: 'Custom version command to run (defaults to "callisto version")'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto version'
  commit_message:
    description: 'Commit message for the Version PR'
    required: false
    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
  title:
    description: 'Title for the Version PR'
    required: false
    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
  pr_label:
    description: 'Label to attach to the Version Packages Pull Request'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto: release'
  create_github_release:
    description: 'Whether to create GitHub Release entries for calculated tags'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  setup_git_user:
    description: 'Whether to automatically configure git user.name and user.email'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  branch:
    description: 'Base branch for Version PRs'
    required: false
    default: 'main'
  cwd:
    description: 'Working directory path if workspace is in a subfolder'
    required: false
    default: '.'

outputs:
  hasChangesets:
    description: 'Whether pending changesets were found'
    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.hasChangesets }}
  published:
    description: 'Whether packages were published'
    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.published }}
  publishedPackages:
    description: 'JSON list of published packages'
    value: ${{ steps.callisto-orchestrate.outputs.publishedPackages }}

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Setup Callisto Environment
      uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto

    - name: Orchestrate Version PR or Publish
      id: callisto-orchestrate
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_PUBLISH: ${{ inputs.publish }}
        INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.version_command }}
        INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE: ${{ inputs.commit_message }}
        INPUT_TITLE: ${{ inputs.title }}
        INPUT_PR_LABEL: ${{ inputs.pr_label }}
        INPUT_CREATE_GITHUB_RELEASE: ${{ inputs.create_github_release }}
        INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER: ${{ inputs.setup_git_user }}
        INPUT_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.branch }}
        INPUT_CWD: ${{ inputs.cwd }}
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ env.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        NPM_TOKEN: ${{ env.NPM_TOKEN }}
        CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ env.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
        TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ env.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      run: |
        set -e
        if [[ "$INPUT_CWD" != "." ]]; then
          cd "$INPUT_CWD"
        fi

        echo "::group::1. Inspecting Workspace Status"
        set +e
        callisto status --check
        STATUS_EXIT=$?
        set -e
        if [[ $STATUS_EXIT -eq 1 ]]; then
          HAS_CHANGESETS=true
        elif [[ $STATUS_EXIT -eq 2 ]]; then
          HAS_CHANGESETS=false
        else
          echo "::error::callisto status --check exited with unexpected code $STATUS_EXIT (expected 1 for pending changesets or 2 for none pending)"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "::endgroup::"

        if [[ "$HAS_CHANGESETS" == "true" ]]; then
          echo "hasChangesets=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "published=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          EXISTING_PR_BODY=$(gh pr list --head callisto/version-packages --json body --jq '.[0].body // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)

          echo "::group::2. Composing Version PR Body"
          if [[ -n "$EXISTING_PR_BODY" ]]; then
            PR_BODY=$(echo "$EXISTING_PR_BODY" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
          else
            PR_BODY=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
          fi
          echo "$PR_BODY"
          echo "::endgroup::"

          echo "::group::3. Bumping Package Versions ($INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND)"
          read -ra _version_cmd <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
          "${_version_cmd[@]}"
          echo "::endgroup::"

          echo "::group::4. Creating / Updating Version Packages Pull Request"
          if [[ -n $(git status --porcelain) ]]; then
            if [[ "$INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER" == "true" ]]; then
              git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
              git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
            fi

            git checkout -B callisto/version-packages
            git add -A
            git commit -m "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE"
            git push origin callisto/version-packages --force

            if [[ -n "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" ]]; then
              gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color "0e8a16" --description "Release packages" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi

            EXISTING_PR=$(gh pr list --head callisto/version-packages --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
            if [[ -n "$EXISTING_PR" ]]; then
              gh pr edit "$EXISTING_PR" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" || true
              if [[ -n "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" ]]; then
                gh pr edit "$EXISTING_PR" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" || true
              fi
            else
              if [[ -n "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" ]]; then
                gh pr create --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" --head callisto/version-packages --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" || gh pr create --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" --head callisto/version-packages --base "$INPUT_BRANCH"
              else
                gh pr create --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$PR_BODY" --head callisto/version-packages --base "$INPUT_BRANCH"
              fi
            fi

            echo "### Version Packages PR Created/Updated" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            echo "$PR_BODY" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          fi
          echo "::endgroup::"
        else
          echo "hasChangesets=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Emit native matrix targets for downstream build jobs, deduplicated
          # by artifactName in case the same triple is declared by more than
          # one package's platform-target group. set -o pipefail ensures a
          # hard `callisto matrix` error (e.g. malformed manifest, conflicting
          # platform-target sources) fails this step instead of silently
          # producing empty output.
          set -o pipefail
          NATIVE_MATRIX=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)') || { echo "::error::callisto matrix failed"; exit 1; }
          echo "nativeMatrix=$NATIVE_MATRIX" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          echo "::group::2. Calculating Topological Publish Plan"
          PLAN_JSON=$(callisto plan-publish --format json)
          echo "$PLAN_JSON"
          echo "::endgroup::"

          # A single source of truth for "nothing to publish this run" --
          # mirrors PublishPlan::is_empty() so this can never drift from what
          # the CLI itself considers empty.
          if echo "$PLAN_JSON" | jq -e '(.rustCrates + .npmPlatformPackages + .npmMainPackages + (.pypiPackages // []) + .releases) | length == 0' > /dev/null; then
            PLAN_IS_EMPTY=true
          else
            PLAN_IS_EMPTY=false
          fi

          if [[ "$PLAN_IS_EMPTY" == "true" ]]; then
            echo "published=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "Nothing to publish this run (no changesets pending, or no package has a pending release)."
          else
          if [[ -n "$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" ]]; then
            echo "::group::Placing Native Build Artifacts"
            while IFS=$'\t' read -r ARTIFACT DIR_RAW; do
              DIR="."
              if [[ -n "$DIR_RAW" ]]; then
                DIR="$DIR_RAW"
              fi
              mkdir -p "$DIR"
              gh run download "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --name "$ARTIFACT" --dir "$DIR" || { echo "::error::failed to download artifact '$ARTIFACT' for placement into '$DIR' within run $GITHUB_RUN_ID"; exit 1; }
            done < <(printf '%s' "$NATIVE_MATRIX" | jq -r '.[] | [.artifactName, (.packageDir | if . == null then "null" else . end)] | @tsv')
            echo "::endgroup::"

            # Wire NPM_TOKEN into npm config so npm publish can authenticate.
            # NPM_TOKEN is forwarded explicitly in this step's env: block so it
            # is available regardless of how the caller sets it.
            if [[ -n "$NPM_TOKEN" ]]; then
              npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken "$NPM_TOKEN"
            fi

            echo "::group::3. Executing Package Publishing"
            if [[ "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "true" ]]; then
              echo "Executing custom publish script: $INPUT_PUBLISH"
              read -ra _publish_cmd <<< "$INPUT_PUBLISH"
              "${_publish_cmd[@]}"
              PUBLISH_EXIT=0
            else
              set +e
              REPORT_JSON=$(callisto publish --format json)
              PUBLISH_EXIT=$?
              set -e
              echo "$REPORT_JSON"
              # Narrow PLAN_JSON down to what the report confirms actually
              # published, so a single package's failure doesn't cost its
              # already-succeeded siblings a tag or a GitHub Release below.
              # Not possible for a custom publish script -- there is no
              # structured report to filter by, so PLAN_JSON is left as-is
              # in that branch (unchanged, pre-existing behaviour).
              PLAN_JSON=$(callisto filter-plan --plan "$PLAN_JSON" --report "$REPORT_JSON" --format json)
            fi
            echo "::endgroup::"

            echo "published=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "publishedPackages<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "$PLAN_JSON" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            if echo "$PLAN_JSON" | jq -e '(.rustCrates + .npmPlatformPackages + .npmMainPackages + (.pypiPackages // []) + .releases) | length == 0' > /dev/null; then
              echo "No packages in this run actually published successfully; skipping tag/release creation."
            else
              echo "::group::4. Tagging Release Commits & Updating Major Version Pointer Aliases"
              set +e
              TAG_REPORT_JSON=$(callisto tag --plan "$PLAN_JSON" --floating-major --format json)
              TAG_EXIT=$?
              set -e
              if [[ $TAG_EXIT -ne 0 ]]; then
                echo "::error::callisto tag failed (exit $TAG_EXIT): $TAG_REPORT_JSON"
              else
                echo "$TAG_REPORT_JSON"
                # Only the floating major-version alias (e.g. `v1`) is meant to
                # move once created -- force-pushing it is correct. An
                # immutable per-version release tag must never be force-moved;
                # pushing it plainly lets git's own non-fast-forward check
                # catch a genuine conflict instead of silently overwriting it.
                IMMUTABLE_TAGS=()
                while IFS= read -r line; do
                  [[ -n "$line" ]] && IMMUTABLE_TAGS+=("$line")
                done < <(echo "$TAG_REPORT_JSON" | jq -r '.tags[] | select(.isFloatingMajor == false) | .tagName')
                FLOATING_TAGS=()
                while IFS= read -r line; do
                  [[ -n "$line" ]] && FLOATING_TAGS+=("$line")
                done < <(echo "$TAG_REPORT_JSON" | jq -r '.tags[] | select(.isFloatingMajor == true) | .tagName')

                if (( ${#IMMUTABLE_TAGS[@]} > 0 )); then
                  git push origin "${IMMUTABLE_TAGS[@]}"
                fi
                if (( ${#FLOATING_TAGS[@]} > 0 )); then
                  git push origin --force "${FLOATING_TAGS[@]}"
                fi
              fi
              echo "::endgroup::"

              if [[ "$INPUT_CREATE_GITHUB_RELEASE" == "true" ]]; then
                echo "::group::5. Creating GitHub Release Entries"
                while IFS=$'\t' read -r TAG HAS_VALID_PRERELEASE IS_PRERELEASE; do
                  [[ -z "$TAG" ]] && continue

                  if [[ "$HAS_VALID_PRERELEASE" != "true" ]]; then
                    echo "::error::release entry for tag $TAG has a missing or non-boolean isPrerelease field"
                    exit 1
                  fi

                  echo "Creating GitHub Release for tag: $TAG"

                  EXTRA_FLAGS=""
                  if [[ "$IS_PRERELEASE" == "true" ]]; then
                    EXTRA_FLAGS="--prerelease"
                  fi

                  gh release create "$TAG" --title "$TAG" --generate-notes $EXTRA_FLAGS || true
                done < <(echo "$PLAN_JSON" | jq -r '.releases[]? | [.tagName, (has("isPrerelease") and (.isPrerelease|type=="boolean")), (.isPrerelease // false)] | @tsv')
                echo "::endgroup::"
              fi

              echo "### Packages Published Successfully" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
            fi

            if [[ $PUBLISH_EXIT -ne 0 ]]; then
              echo "::error::callisto publish reported one or more failures; see the report above"
              exit 1
            fi
          else
            echo "published=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "No changesets pending and no publish command provided."
          fi
          fi
        fi
name: Release & Publish Workflow

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify CI Pipeline (Format, Lint, Test, WASM, Security Audit)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install Toolchain & Cache
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@v2

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

  release:
    name: Version Packages or Publish Release
    needs: [verify]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      statuses: write
      checks: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Install Toolchain
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-callisto

      - name: Run Callisto Release Action
        uses: ./.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          publish: "true"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN || secrets.CARGO_TOKEN || secrets.CRATES_IO_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

    },

The diagnostic reports the expected digest (from the job output), the computed digest, and the byte length of the file received. The same termination applies when the artifact is missing, when it contains a number of files other than one, or when `envelope_digest` is empty or absent from the plan job's outputs; in none of those cases does the execute job proceed to validation, recompute a plan, or continue with a partially trusted file.",
      "is_error_case": true
    },
    {
      "id": "AC-003",
      "criterion": "Plans are emitted only on an explicit request.   "implementation_notes": [
